setting: You three sit on the committee of a village football club in the northern Lake District, in Cumbria, where the pitch is on the edge of the fells and the club has run for about forty years. You know each other from committee meetings, Saturday matches and the clubhouse bar, and you have worked together for several seasons. You know roughly where each other lives and works, and you are aware of each other's usual habits. The last thing you talked about in the group was whether the rain had flooded the lower field again.
opener: Asking the group to confirm who is bringing the cash box to Saturday's match.

Ruth.knows: You know Gary is the treasurer, a man you have worked with for years and trust with the money. You know Chloe is the fixtures officer, a younger woman who joined the committee two seasons ago and runs the match schedule well.
Ruth.like: You are measured and methodical, and you keep things in order without fuss. You have a dry sense of humour and strong views on people who turn up late to meetings and on the state of the village car park.
Ruth.texts: You message the group now and then without being asked, mostly to pass on club admin.
Ruth.style: You type in full sentences with capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Gary.knows: You know Ruth is the secretary, a sensible woman who keeps the club's paperwork in order and whom you have known for a long time. You know Chloe is the fixtures officer, a younger member you respect for getting things done quickly.
Gary.like: You are easygoing and blunt, with a loud laugh and a habit of teasing people you like. You have strong opinions about referees, the price of materials and whether the club should spend money on new goalposts.
Gary.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when money or pitch matters come up.
Gary.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation and often use a thumbs-up emoji.

Chloe.knows: You know Ruth is the secretary, an older woman who keeps the club's records and is very particular about deadlines. You know Gary is the treasurer, a man who likes to talk about money and will tease you about it.
Chloe.like: You are energetic and quick-witted, and you get frustrated by disorganisation but laugh at yourself easily. You have opinions about fixture clashes, the quality of the village pitch and which local pub does the best chips.
Chloe.texts: You message the group mostly when there is a fixture to sort, otherwise you stay quiet.
Chloe.style: You type in lowercase or mixed case with frequent abbreviations and the occasional laughing emoji.

private_lines.Ruth: You live in a stone house on the edge of a village near Keswick, and you retired from a job in a council office a few years ago. You live with your husband, Mike, who is a keen walker, and your mornings usually start with a walk on the fell path before you sort the post and the club paperwork at the kitchen table.
private_lines.Gary: You live in a terraced house in the village and work as a self-employed plasterer, travelling to jobs across the valley. You live alone with a lurcher called Bess, and your days start early with site work and finish with a pint at the clubhouse when the weather allows.
private_lines.Chloe: You live in a rented flat in the village with a flatmate and work as a nurse at the hospital in Carlisle, so your shifts are spread across the week and you often commute by car. Your days are busy and practical, with the shifts, a run when you can and time at the clubhouse on match days.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

text: Can someone confirm who is bringing the cash box to Saturday's match. Last time it went missing in the car for an hour.
me. i'll have it in the van. dont let chloe near it she'll put it on the bar
lol excuse me. i put it on the bar ONCE
Once is enough. Gary, you'll need to hand over the float as well, I've put it on the agenda for the meeting.
float is in the tin already. dont fuss ruth
on another note, are we still playing the Ambleside away on the 6th or is that moved again
Moved to the 13th. It's on the revised list I sent out last Thursday. Check your email.
ah yes. sorry. been on nights all week, my brain is mush
nights? you lot get paid for sleeping at work
gary you have never once been in a hospital at 3am and it shows
fair. i was in a loft in kendal at 3am once with a dead rat and a bucket of hot tar. different hell
Gary, the pitch booking for the 13th needs paying by Friday or we lose the slot. Can you sort it from the account?
Morning. Ambleside have sent the referee details for the 13th. I'll forward them to the group.
ta. ooh can someone tell me what chips the pub in ambleside does. important info
the ones that come in a bag. dont go to the one by the lake, theyre cold
i'm sleeping now, reply later if it's important 😴
pitch is waterlogged again down the lower end. ruth can you chase the council
I'll write to them tomorrow. They take a week to answer anything so don't expect a quick fix.
Gary, have you got the ground staff rota sorted for Saturday? Last year we had nobody on the gate until half two.
yeah its sorted. dave and the lad from the garage. dont need a spreadsheet ruth
I'll have the spreadsheet regardless. Thank you.
right, ambleside away on the 13th. kick off 2pm? they wanted 2:30 last time so check
Kick off 2pm as per the revised list. Ambleside have confirmed.
👍 just checking. the 2:30 thing was a nightmare
Morning. Walked up to the tarn before the rain came in. Lower field will be underwater again, I'd put money on it.
its always underwater. im on a job in windermere till 4. ill look at it after
just woke up. did anyone chase the council about the drainage or is that still on ruth
I wrote to them yesterday. Auto reply says five working days.
five working days is basically a yes
just got back. lower end is a lake. bess has already decided its hers
dont tell ruth i said lake
I can read, Gary.
